validation.cross_crate_print_scope: Parallel compiler output may interleave; selected complete blocks pass size checks and root/source-qualified repeated task records agree. Unqualified names that collide across crates are not merged.
validation.generator_variant_arithmetic_scope: Raw field/padding lists may overlap a discriminant byte. Type checks use top-level tags/padding plus maximum declared variant size; raw details remain available.

interpretation: The main permanent frame is dominated by the active session variant, not the already boxed handshake or join setup.
Writer and select tuple are nested within the session future, which is nested within the outer future and task cell. These sizes must not be summed as independent allocations.
The separate capsule task has its own cell and parser future. Removing its cell while retaining that future elsewhere is relocation; compute the enlarged main task and every surviving owner.

Both current outer and capsule futures are below even Tokio debug boxing threshold2048 and release threshold16384. The boxed-cell context records represent alternate generic branches, not an extra persistent allocation in these spawn calls.

Application types are identified by source location or complete qualified function identity. Unqualified frame::Frame names collide across crates and are not merged. Root/source-qualified repeated records agree numerically.

Exact structure sums and tag-plus-max-declared-variant sums are checked. Raw generator variant field/padding sums can differ by a discriminant byte due to offset/discriminant placement; they are retained rather than misreported as disjoint fields.

Cross-crate output can interleave in a parallel cargo build. Selected complete blocks pass size checks and repeated root types agree; this does not authenticate every unselected block in the full log.
The diagnostic binary differs from the ordinary selected release and is not an ordinary benchmark executable. Requested-live heap is historical selected-image evidence, not a fresh census.
Final Initial/Handshake packet-space retirement already removed 1072 inline bytes and remains retained.
Optional previous-path boxing was already rejected after a paced reliable failure; do not repeat unchanged.
Compact RNG storage was already rejected after private/room throughput regressions.
Streams704, Data-space544, statistics536, current-path408 and peer-parameters352 are live state, not one unused slab.
Untried independent cold-metadata targets are individually much smaller than 1KiB per connection.

Replacing Quinn driver/wrapper alone can remove at most its 688 inline bytes before replacement state costs; the 4656-byte protocol owner remains. Real savings require fewer or smaller owned states, not boxing them.

A major combined store/driver redesign must also remove duplicated per-connection dispatch/wakeup/map/task allocations and preserve stream, congestion, timer, FIFO and cancellation semantics; aggregate savings require actual heap proof.

next_candidate_status.established_session_core: Unmeasured representation proposal only. Its required state, new cells/boxes, Output/IO growth and independent routing/writer progress must all be counted before any saving claim.
next_candidate_status.recommendation: Prototype one owned established SessionCore representation that polls the existing writer/read/route state without retaining nested async maxima and duplicate captures. Keep one application task, independent stream/datagram routing continuations and writer progress, all budgets/deadlines/cancellation semantics, and existing capsule behavior. First measure total task plus all persistent owners; a setup box, moved writer state, extra task, or merged capsule alone is not the proposed saving.
avoid_repeating: Cold handshake boxing is already retained; current peak is established state.
A smaller task allocation plus a separately boxed live future is not a total-owner saving.
Capsule fusion retains required receive/parser state and changes construction/admission/teardown ownership.
Previous-path boxing, compact RNG and grouped Quinn-driver experiments have recorded rejections; their unchanged candidates are not proposed again.

limits: No runtime benchmark or candidate memory-saving experiment was performed for this report.
The 5344-byte Arc allocation contains the 4656-byte protocol object; these are nested ownership and cannot be added as separate allocations.
The 688-byte wrapper is a ceiling on deleting that existing inline wrapper before replacement state; protocol state and separately owned channel/task/map allocations remain.
Large protocol members include live stream, packet-space, path, timer, statistics and peer state; their sizes alone do not establish cold or removable storage.
A changed allocator, future representation or owner boundary needs a net requested-live/RSS comparison and complete ordinary behavior/performance acceptance.
This capture excludes later parent-owned candidate builds, tests, heap screens and timings. Those require their own source and outcome reports.
